name: Battle of the Bagradas River
intro: An open plain near Tunis, in the First Punic War. You are the consul Regulus with 15,000 infantry and 500 cavalry. The Carthaginians, led in the field by the Spartan Xanthippus, have 12,000 infantry, 4,000 cavalry and 100 elephants.
debrief: In reality, the Carthaginians fought on level ground that suited their cavalry and elephants. Regulus massed his legionaries in a deep, dense centre, with a short front. The Roman cavalry was swept away, and part of the Roman left overlapped the elephants and routed the Carthaginian right, but the pursuers left the battle. The rest of the infantry struggled with the elephants and were attacked from the rear by the returning cavalry. Xanthippus then ordered the phalanx forward, and most Romans were killed in their packed formation. About 13,000 Romans died, about 2,000 escaped to Aspis, and Regulus was captured with about 500 men. Carthaginian records were destroyed in 146 BC, so the account rests mainly on a Greek historian, whom modern historians largely accept. Holding broken ground and the lane and wide-line tactics are what-ifs.

win: Your columns reach the hills with the army intact.
The Carthaginian phalanx cannot catch them.
Xanthippus is left holding an empty plain.
lose: The phalanx closes on the packed Romans.
Regulus and a handful break out and are run down.

options.text: Wide line, cavalry on both ends

decisions.title: Where to fight
decisions.text: Carthage has hired the Spartan Xanthippus, who wants a battle on open ground. You have 15,000 infantry and only 500 cavalry. You were told to wear Carthage down by raids.

hint.text: The Carthaginians have many elephants and cavalry. Open ground favours both.

scout.text: Elephants and cavalry are weak on broken ground. Raids and local recruits fit your orders; a battle on the plain fits Xanthippus.

choices.label: Advance onto the open plain and offer battle

fx.text: You march onto a level plain, exactly where the Carthaginian cavalry and elephants are strongest.

choices.label: Hold the broken ground at the plain’s edge and raid

fx.text: The Carthaginians must come to you across rough ground, which slows their elephants and cavalry.

choices.label: Send for recruits from the rebel towns and delay

fx.text: More men arrive, but the Carthaginians gain time too.

decisions.title: Your formation
decisions.text: Your 500 horse are outnumbered eight to one. A deep centre is strong against the phalanx but short on the flanks.

hint.text: The Carthaginian cavalry will sweep round a short front.

scout.text: A deep, dense centre has a short front and open flanks. A wider, shallower line with the cavalry guarding the ends keeps the flanks covered.

choices.label: Mass the legions deep to smash the phalanx

fx.text: The legions form a deep, dense centre. The front is short.

choices.label: Keep a wider line, cavalry guarding both ends

fx.text: The line is longer, with cavalry on each flank.

choices.label: Anchor one flank on the rough ground

fx.text: One flank is covered, but the other is open.

decisions.title: The elephants
decisions.text: A hundred elephants stand in front of the Carthaginian centre. Behind them come the phalanx and the cavalry.

hint.text: The elephants are in a single line, with no infantry in front of them.

scout.text: Elephants follow open lanes. Beating shields frightens them, but lanes and javelins turn them aside.

choices.label: Advance banging swords on shields to scare them

fx.text: The noise frightens some elephants, but most come on.
The elephants trample the front ranks.

choices.label: Open lanes in the maniples and let them through

fx.text: The elephants run through the lanes and the velites harry them.

decisions.title: The left wing overlaps
decisions.text: On your left, part of the line overlaps the elephants and routs the Carthaginian right. The pursuers run toward the enemy camp.

hint.text: The Carthaginian right is in flight.

scout.text: Pursuers who run to the camp are out of the battle. Brought back, they can strike the phalanx’s flank.

choices.label: Let the allies chase the beaten wing to its camp

fx.text: The pursuit takes your best men out of the battle.

choices.label: Recall them and wheel against the phalanx

fx.text: Your line is wide enough to turn. The allies hit the phalanx in the flank.
The allies wheel, but your dense centre cannot keep up.
They hold, but the chance passes.

decisions.title: The cavalry returns
decisions.text: The Carthaginian cavalry, having swept your horse away, comes back against your rear and flanks.

hint.text: Dust rises on both flanks and behind.

scout.text: A rear guard facing the cavalry costs fighting strength in front. Pressing on leaves the rear open.

choices.label: Press on and break the phalanx before they arrive

fx.text: You press forward, but the cavalry hits your rear and flanks.

choices.label: Turn a rear guard to face the cavalry

fx.text: The wider line has the depth to turn a rear rank about. The cavalry cannot ride in.
The rear guard turns the cavalry, but the front is weakened.

choices.label: Withdraw toward the hills in good order

fx.text: You pull back and keep the army together, but lose the field.

decisions.title: The phalanx
decisions.text: Xanthippus orders the phalanx forward against the packed Romans, with elephants and cavalry pressing in.

hint.text: The phalanx is advancing in step.

scout.text: A packed army cannot fight in all directions. Two columns can break out through a weaker screen toward the hills.

choices.label: Stand and receive the phalanx where you are

fx.text: The packed Romans are slaughtered where they stand.

choices.label: Break out in two columns toward the hills

fx.text: Two columns cut through the weaker screen and reach the foothills, hurting the Carthaginians as they go.

choices.label: Form a hollow square and hold

fx.text: The square holds for a time, but it cannot move.

sources.title: Battle of the Bagradas River, 255 BC (Wikipedia)
